stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: After nearly a century of heavy truck traffic, the Harlan River suspension bridge was expected to need its main cables replaced. When engineers finally inspected the steel strands up close, however, they found almost no corrosion and only slight fraying near the anchorages. The cables turned out to be far less ______ than the inspection team had predicted, and the replacement project was postponed indefinitely.
explanation: The evidence says the cables were in good condition: almost no corrosion and only slight fraying. The phrase "far less ______" reverses that, so the blank has to be the opposite of good condition. "Deteriorated" fits: the cables were far less worn than expected, which is why the replacement was put off.

A.why: You matched the blank directly to the evidence (the cables held up well) and skipped the word "less." Saying the cables were "far less durable" than predicted means they were in worse shape, which is the opposite of what the inspection found.

C.why: You picked a word people often use about bridges. The passage is about the cables' physical condition, not their appearance, so "elegant" has nothing to do with the inspection findings.

D.why: You grabbed onto the mention of heavy truck traffic. The blank describes the cables, and cables can't be "congested." The sentence is about wear, not traffic.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When a small tremor shook the Arroyo Valley last spring, many residents worried that it signaled a larger earthquake on the way. Seismologists who studied the valley's main fault reached a calmer conclusion. The fault has been quiet for centuries, and instruments placed along it since the tremor show no sign of strain building up. A major earthquake there, the researchers reported, is unlikely to be ______.
explanation: The evidence says the fault is quiet and no strain is building, so a big quake is not coming soon. The phrase "unlikely to be" denies the blank, so the blank has to mean "coming soon." "Imminent" fits: a major quake is unlikely to be imminent.

B.why: You matched the blank to the evidence (a quake is far off) and skipped the reversal in "unlikely to be." Saying a quake is "unlikely to be distant" means it is probably close, which is the opposite of what the seismologists concluded.

C.why: You were thinking of how an earthquake feels or sounds. Whether a quake makes noise has nothing to do with the strain data or the residents' worry about timing.

D.why: The sentence already calls the earthquake "major," so saying it is unlikely to be "minor" just repeats that point. It doesn't tell you anything about the fault being quiet, which is what the evidence is about.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Historians long dismissed the hand-drawn charts of the Calder coastline, made by sixteenth-century pilots, as little more than rough sketches. A recent study that laid the charts over modern satellite images challenges the view that they were ______: most of the bays, river mouths, and headlands the pilots recorded sit within a few hundred meters of their true positions.
explanation: The satellite comparison shows that the charts were accurate. The study "challenges the view" in the blank, so the blank has to be the opposite of accurate. "Inaccurate" fits: the study pushes back on the old belief that the charts were wrong.

A.why: You matched the blank to what the study found (the charts are accurate) and missed "challenges the view that." A study can't challenge the view that the charts were precise while also showing that they are precise.

B.why: You picked a word people associate with old maps. The study tested where features were placed, not how the charts looked, so "decorative" isn't the view the evidence knocks down.

D.why: The passage says the charts date from the sixteenth century, and the study has nothing to do with when they were made. "Recent" clashes with the stated date and has no connection to the satellite evidence.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: For her series of harbor scenes, printmaker Ines Navarro carves every woodblock herself and applies ink to it with a hand roller before pressing each sheet by hand. Because the ink never spreads the same way twice, small differences in tone and texture show up from one impression to the next. Her method therefore precludes ______ copies, and collectors value each print as a slightly different version of the image.
explanation: The evidence says every impression comes out a little different. "Precludes" means "rules out," so the blank has to be what the method makes impossible: copies that are exactly the same. "Identical" fits.

A.why: You were thinking of paper prints in general. Nothing in the passage says the prints break easily, and hand inking doesn't stop a print from being fragile.

B.why: You matched the blank to the evidence (each print differs) and skipped "precludes." A method that rules out distinct copies would make every print the same, which is the opposite of what the passage describes.

C.why: You assumed that handmade work affects price. The passage never mentions cost, and nothing about uneven ink would rule out expensive copies.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Forecasters had warned that Tropical Storm Della would stall over the coast and bring three days of heavy rain and flooding. Instead, the storm turned offshore within hours of making landfall, and most towns in its path recorded less than a centimeter of drizzle. For those communities, Della proved to be little more than a ______ disturbance.
explanation: The evidence is that Della turned out much weaker than forecast and brought only light drizzle. "Little more than" shrinks whatever follows it, so the blank should describe something small. "Minor" fits: Della was hardly more than a minor disturbance.

B.why: You matched the blank to the forecast of heavy rain and flooding and ignored both "instead" and "little more than." The storm turned out weak, so calling it "severe" reverses what actually happened.

C.why: You picked a weather word because the passage is about weather. "Humid" doesn't express how weak the storm turned out to be, which is the point of "little more than."

D.why: "Historic" suggests an exceptional event, but the storm brought less than a centimeter of drizzle. The phrase "little more than" plays the storm down, and "historic" does the opposite.
